definition: involving a lot of effort; difficult and tiring
memoryTip: Hard work that makes you say “argh!” — arduous = exhausting effort.
correctPassage: The creation of the first feature-length animated film was an arduous process that took years of frame-by-frame work.
wrongPassages: The walk to the mailbox was called arduous though it took twelve effortless seconds.
He described the nap as arduous because he fell asleep at once and woke rested.
One-click install was marketed as an arduous journey through expert menus.

memoryTip: In + consequence → without consequences → doesn’t matter.
correctPassage: Whether the monarch’s reign was considered historically significant or relatively inconsequential, questions of legitimacy still shaped its course.
wrongPassages: The truce was inconsequential the morning shells fell on both capitals.
Leadership hoped to inconsequential attrition metrics by changing the formula mid-year.
The witness gave an inconsequential timeline that matched the footage minute by minute.

memoryTip: In-superable: you can’t “get over” it (like an unsuperable wall).
correctPassage: Insuperable though the conjecture seemed to many mathematicians, it eventually yielded to a rigorous proof.
wrongPassages: The injunction was insuperable on its face and needed no later clarification.
The secondary theme was insuperable and never interacted with the tonic.
Lenders avoided the insuperable borrower who had never missed a payment.

definition: an opinion formed without complete evidence; a guess
memoryTip: Con + jecture (throw) → throw out a guess without full proof.
correctPassage: Before the spacecraft’s flyby, scientists could only conjecture about the composition of the planet’s atmosphere.
wrongPassages: She favorite-starred pin conjecture and navigated there every Tuesday by habit.
She inked the keg conjecture and packed spare badges only.
The gold-seal conjecture form had signature lines and no clauses.

definition: relating to what did not happen but might have; contrary to fact
memoryTip: Counter + fact → against what actually happened; “what if?” history.
correctPassage: The essay explores a counterfactual scenario: what if the treaty had never been signed?
wrongPassages: Voters buried the counterfactual bond that engineers called urgent.
She packed a counterfactual suitcase: one shirt and a book for a month abroad.
The mall’s counterfactual daylight film turned every storefront the same amber.

definition: the ability to produce a desired result
memoryTip: Sounds like “effective-acy” — does it actually work?
correctPassage: A controlled trial was designed to test the efficacy of the new teaching method against standard instruction.
wrongPassages: Boards tabled the efficacy proposal community letters had supported.
The ice ramp felt efficacy after crews salted it like a city sidewalk.
Committees shelved the efficacy pilot users had rated highest overall.

memoryTip: Rect- as in correct/rectangle (straight) → make it right again.
correctPassage: Editors worked overnight to rectify factual errors that had slipped into the first edition.
wrongPassages: The watcher will rectify the page by routing it to a channel nobody reads.
Doctors did not rectify the pain; they increased the dose that caused it.
They tried to rectify the spam by unsubscribing from nothing and clicking every link.

memoryTip: Like accent — put the accent on it so it stands out more.
correctPassage: Harsh lighting served only to accentuate the cracks already visible in the statue’s surface.
wrongPassages: They hoped to accentuate the walkout story by calling it a “team building absence.”
He tried to accentuate the injunction by using a shell company for the same sales.
She hoped to accentuate the walkout risk by ignoring the petition’s signatures.

memoryTip: When the moon eclipses the sun, it covers it — or one star outshines another.
correctPassage: The younger novelist’s success threatened to eclipse her mentor’s long-established reputation.
wrongPassages: The slip’s eclipse freeboard marks were worn down to bare metal.
Committees cut the eclipse translation budget that clinics still needed.
Committees shelved the eclipse pilot that had the highest user rating.

memoryTip: Man-ifest: so clear a man could “fist” it / obvious on the face of it.
correctPassage: The benefits of the reform were soon manifest in higher graduation rates across the district.
wrongPassages: a manifest tabletop report is a photo of the whiteboard after it was wiped.
Funds chased manifest yield in a product that never paid a coupon.
The rupture disc was manifest: rated above the header’s design pressure.

memoryTip: Pre-vail: come out on top; the stronger idea “wins.”
correctPassage: Despite early setbacks, optimism continued to prevail among the research team.
wrongPassages: The subtonic held was prevail under a final major triad on I.
The safety valve was prevail and never lifted during the pressure test.
The speech was prevail in the sense that it never risked a single contested claim.

memoryTip: Re-pudiate: push away / refuse to own it — “I repudiate that claim.”
correctPassage: The senator moved quickly to repudiate comments that misrepresented the committee’s findings.
wrongPassages: She hoped to repudiate the walkout by requiring a loyalty pledge at the door.
They tried to repudiate the flood story by renaming street water as “misting.”
They tried to repudiate the mold by covering vents with plastic sheets.

memoryTip: A buttress props up a wall — so it supports an argument too.
correctPassage: Archival letters buttress her argument that the inventor knew of earlier designs.
wrongPassages: The wharf’s buttress crane load chart was for equipment long since scrapped.
The ascent felt buttress inside a pressurized cabin to the summit hotel.
Her buttress interrogatory set asked for every email ever sent by anyone.

memoryTip: Miti-gate: open a gate to make the problem milder / less severe.
correctPassage: New regulations were intended to mitigate the environmental damage caused by mining.
wrongPassages: The rules will mitigate harm by doubling penalties and removing safety checks.
She mitigated the ruined soup by adding more of what had spoiled it.
To mitigate attendance, organizers cancelled the event and locked the doors.

memoryTip: Con-strain: keep under strain / squeezed inside limits.
correctPassage: Limited funding will constrain what the laboratory can accomplish this year.
wrongPassages: The savanna looked constrain after fire and rain restarted the grass cycle.
The serac zone felt constrain from a marked snow bridge with fixed ropes.
a constrain load test hits one request and graphs a single point.

memoryTip: A-morph (no shape) — like amorphous blob with no outline.
correctPassage: The plan remained amorphous until the committee agreed on concrete milestones.
wrongPassages: an amorphous majority of one vote was recorded in the minutes as unanimous consent.
His amorphous confidence vanished as soon as the first hard question was asked.
The bass line was amorphous and never locked with the kick drum.

memoryTip: Sounds like “spurious / suspicious” — fake, not genuine.
correctPassage: Later analysis showed that the correlation was spurious, produced by a coding error.
wrongPassages: The station’s spurious platform screen showed yesterday’s departures all day.
The wharf looked spurious at slack tide with a clear open horizon.
Investors wanted spurious markets so prices would never move more than a cent.

memoryTip: Co-roborate: two sources “rob” doubt together — they confirm each other.
correctPassage: A second laboratory’s measurements corroborate the first team’s temperature readings.
wrongPassages: a second lab moved to corroborate the claim by discarding the original data.
She corroborated the rumor by refusing to discuss it with anyone.
The blank page was said to corroborate the model without one measurement.

definition: asserting opinions as if absolutely true
memoryTip: Like a dog that won’t drop the bone — stubborn about “my truth.”
correctPassage: His dogmatic refusal to consider alternative explanations weakened the paper’s credibility.
wrongPassages: The mudflat stayed dogmatic in a tide model locked permanently at low water.
The bay looked dogmatic under foghorns with no hulls visible on the water.
The board’s dogmatic minutes recorded motions, votes, and abstentions in order.

memoryTip: No scruples (moral brakes) — will do anything for gain.
correctPassage: Unscrupulous vendors inflated prices once they realized tourists had no other options.
wrongPassages: His unscrupulous certificate of conference claimed talks that never took place.
Reviewers called the methods unscrupulous once every step could be repeated elsewhere.
His unscrupulous proposed order left the relief section completely blank.
